title: Wren the mender
creator: your-handle
description: A townsperson with no shop: a mender who stands at the trainers' stall, and who speaks of the past only as her gran's saying.

first: Oh, hello! I am Wren. I mend what people bring me: cups, straps, the odd hinge.
This stall was empty when I came. Somebody had left a stool and a lantern.
What have you got in your bag that is cracked?
stranger: Bring me anything with a crack in it. I like to know what it was before.
My gran said the bells ring for what is lost. I only know they ring after dark.
acquaintance: Every mended thing tells me something. A cup mended twice was loved twice.
Whoever laid the old cobbles took care. You can tell by the corners.
friend: You bring me more cracks than anyone. Thank you. I mean it.
Gran also said a town is never mended, only kept. Maru would nod at that.
